\[
q^2 = \frac{\tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(|\nabla I| / I\bigr)^2 - \tfrac{1}{16}\bigl(\nabla^2 I / I\bigr)^2}{\bigl(1 + \tfrac{1}{4}\, \nabla^2 I / I\bigr)^2},
\qquad
c = \frac{1}{1 + \frac{q^2 - q_0^2}{q_0^2 (1 + q_0^2)}},
\qquad
I \leftarrow I + \frac{\Delta t}{4} \operatorname{div}(c\, \nabla I)
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(q\): The instantaneous coefficient of variation
- \(q_0\): The speckle scale
- \(c\): The diffusion coefficient
- \(\Delta t\): The time step

q is the instantaneous coefficient of variation of Yu and Acton, from the differences to the four neighbors. Its square is the sum of the four squared differences, divided by I squared, combined with the sum of the differences, the Laplacian. In speckle, q is close to the speckle scale q0 and the coefficient c is near 1, so the image diffuses. On edges q is large and c is near 0. The divergence uses c at the pixel for the north and west differences, and at the south and east neighbors for the other two. Here c is limited to 0 to 1.
